raw_final_content:
This is a strong image-level match for Oxalis corniculata (creeping woodsorrel / カタバミ). Across all three images the plant repeatedly shows three obcordate, heart-like leaflets with a distinct apical notch, small yellow flowers, and a low prostrate growth habit. The second image is especially useful because the stem is exposed by hand and appears slender and creeping; the third shows the plant forming a mat along the edge.

Other yellow-flowered Oxalis such as O. dillenii or O. stricta are reasonable formal alternatives, but the strongly creeping/mat-forming habit makes O. corniculata the best visual fit. A close photograph of the petiole base/stipules, node rooting and a mature capsule would make the species determination even more secure.
